evals.name: happy-path-unpushed-commits-with-template
evals.prompt: can you open a PR for this branch? I think I forgot to push
evals.fixture: feature branch `feat/imap-starttls`, 3 unpushed commits (2 feat + 1 test, all scoped imap), .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md present, one untracked file in the working tree
evals.expected_output: Pushes the branch with -u, opens a PR into main, title synthesized across all 3 commits (not just the last), body follows the repo template with checklist left unchecked, mentions the untracked file was not included
assertions: git push ran before gh pr create
gh pr create used --base main
PR title references the feature as a whole, not only the final test commit
PR title retains the shared (imap) scope
PR body follows the repo's PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md section headings
template checklist items were left unchecked
body was passed via --body-file rather than inline --body
the untracked file was not committed
response tells the user the untracked file is excluded from the PR

evals.name: on-target-branch-stops-and-asks
evals.prompt: make a PR against main please
evals.fixture: checked out on `main`, 2 commits ahead of origin/main, no other branches
evals.expected_output: Detects it is on the target branch, does NOT rewrite history, proposes a branch name and the move/reset recovery, and waits for confirmation
assertions: no git reset --hard was executed
no new branch was force-created without asking
no gh pr create was attempted
response explains a PR cannot go from main into main
response proposes a concrete branch name derived from the commits
response asks for confirmation before proceeding

evals.name: existing-open-pr-is-reused
evals.prompt: put this branch up for review
evals.fixture: feature branch already pushed, an open PR already exists for it
evals.expected_output: Reports the existing PR URL and does not create a duplicate
assertions: gh pr create was NOT called
response reports the existing PR URL
response states no duplicate was created

evals.name: mixed-scope-title-synthesis-no-template
evals.fixture: branch with 4 commits across different scopes (feat(db), refactor(scheduler), docs, fix(db)), no PR template in the repo
evals.expected_output: Title names the overall capability and drops the misleading single scope; body uses the fallback Summary/Commits/Test plan structure
assertions: PR title does not use a scope that covers only part of the change
PR title describes the capability rather than listing steps
body contains Summary, Commits, and Test plan sections
body lists all 4 commit subjects
body ends with the Claude Code attribution line
